To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

gamma-irradiated animals show a transient stimulation of the synthesis of ribonucleie acids in regenerating liver, but not in normal liver, and that the synthesis of ribosome RNA is stimulated, whereas that of messenger RNA is not.
the synthesis of ribosome RNA in rat liver cells is enhanced by gamma-irradiating the animals.
the synthesis of pre-mRNAs in regenerating rat livers was suppressed by irradiation, while the synthesis of pre-ribosomal RNAs was not.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of ionizing irradiation on the early events in the biosynthesis of different RNA types.
the study of the effects of ionizing radiation and of partial hepatectomy on the synthesis of RNA in normal and regenarating rat liver.
the effects of ionizing radiation on the biosynthesis of different kinds of RNA in rat liver.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the early effects of ionizing radiation on RNA metabolism in regenerating liver is similar to that in normal liver, and the early increase in pre-rRNA synthesis is not specific for regenerating tissue.
irradiation stimulates the early synthesis of pre-rRNAs and pre-mRNAs in the normal liver and of pre-rRNPs in the regenerating liver.
irradiation of the whole body of rats with 4 krad of gamma-irradation does not affect the synthesis of pre-mRNAs in the liver, but enhances the synthesis of pre-RNA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the early inhibition of the synthesis of heterogeneous RNA after irradiation of regenerating liver is due to an inhibition of cellular programming.
the synthesis of pre-mRNAs and of pre-rRNAs is enhanced in the first hours after the exposure of the liver to ionizing radiation.
the synthesis of RNA precursors is not a specific cellular response to partial hepatectomy.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the early increase of ribosomal RNA synthesis is a non-specific response of the cell to different injuring factors, while the early increase of heterogeneous nuclear RNA is specific for regeneration.
the synthesis of pre-RNA in the liver of irradiated animals is not inhibited but rather enhanced, at least during the early post-irradiation period.
ionizing radiation can affect the biosynthesis of different RNA types in a different way.
